provider_contract.binding: The table and context are captured once only after successful admission. No binding refresh at dispatch or after nested return. Context may be NULL if the selected authored callback accepts it; the planned runtime harness uses actual live nonnull contexts. A pointer is not dereferenced merely to validate it.
provider_contract.branch_local_validation: Immediately before each required dispatch, test the captured table and the reached function pointer. Missing required table/function halts Active/INCOMPLETE without a callback return, raw-available state for that operation, authoritative returned receipt or public completion. Unused callbacks may be NULL: no-owner needs only unblamed; open -1 needs no later callbacks. No global all-functions validator or second admission.
dispatch_order: ac_enter marks the selected event entered, clears raw availability and prepares WRITE length/payload before any required callback.

ac_receive performs one branch-local callback call. An I/O result is assigned immediately by value to a local ac_io_value, then copied into raw.io without any intervening callback or error getter; publish raw.available/AC_RAW_AVAILABLE only after ordinary callback return. Void unblamed gets raw availability only after it returns.

ac_record alone validates returned domains, marks returned_recorded, captures error_number only for raw==-1, and sets independent known_failure/short_write flags. The callback-return pair and this authoritative receipt are different stages.

Only after OPEN has been recorded with nonnegative raw does the next dispatch consume that exact int64_t token from the accepted OPEN receipt; never narrow it to int or treat zero as failure. WRITE/FSYNC/CLOSE use that saved accepted value, never re-call open.
Preserve branch continuation: open -1 completes after OPEN; returned write -1/short still leads to FSYNC then CLOSE; invalid domain halts before recording that event or later calls.

Only after all selected operations return and record does ac_publish_internal copy the complete result then release-store OrdinaryReturned. ac_observe remains acquire-gated and returns no working/raw payload during callbacks.
provider_contract.entry: Retain ac_run(const ac_request *) and its ordinary loop/return mapping. A future request retains pc/lr/fp but replaces authored open/write/sync/close fields with const ap_provider_table *providers and void *context. Only the winning ac_begin_internal path copies those pointer values into private winning bindings after ac_admit_internal succeeds and before driving. NULL request stores NULL bindings without dereference and retains the selected NULL-input failure path. Suppressed callers return before reading any request field, table field or context storage.
provider_contract.errors: failure_errno is an explicitly authored integer returned in the same ac_io_value. It is not a read of ambient errno, errno TLS, native syscall result or retry instruction. Nonfailure return ignores this field in the authoritative receipt. A callback-prepared pair, actual by-value return, private raw capture, authoritative receipt and public completion must not be conflated.
provider_contract.journal: Callbacks append only to their own bounded authored transcript, including invocation kind, context identity and argument values; a journal entry labelled prepared_return is written before the callback's C return and is not itself proof the outer engine captured/recorded it. Completed receipts and exact source/future method review corroborate the path. Incomplete cases expose no private partial state. No private observer/step/inspection/refusal API is added.
provider_contract.lifetime: The outer request/table/registry and callback code remain unchanged throughout the synchronous entry. Context mutation is limited to bounded transcript, nesting guard and recorded public/nested results; no free/unload, table swap, model publication, source request mutation, reset or arbitrary recursion. Repeated-entry tests mutate only caller-owned source values after first return. Winning bindings are not used by suppressed later entries. This is not quiescence or reclamation proof.
provider_contract.nesting: A designated unblamed/open/write callback sets its one-use local nesting flag before making exactly one synchronous ac_run call, with either a distinct stable valid request/table/context or genuine NULL. The nested call must return SUPPRESSED at the same terminal CAS before request/provider access. It neither drives nor changes winning bindings, selector, raw or working state. Callback may call public ac_observe before/after this nested call: Active/no payload. Outer callback then returns its authored value and ordinary outer progression resumes.
provider_contract.nonreturn: Nonreturning/nonlocal callbacks are not executed or modeled as successful returns. Source reasoning leaves the attempt Active and entered-but-no-recorded-return unknown if control never returns; no cleanup, recovery or signal-safety conclusion.
provider_contract.selection: Keep exact six retained reader fragments, selector/cell path, full 64-bit process identity and canonical 33-byte ID unchanged. Complete authored module/generated/cell setup before entry using only the five AO_WITNESS_SETUP APIs. Both commit Virgin checks remain intact. A generated binding is not a module index; per-slot acquires are not a coherent snapshot.
provider_contract.table: One fixed const table per authored context, with typed open/write/sync/close callbacks returning ac_io_value by value and void unblamed(void *context). Callback code and table/context/request/model storage remain live through the outer ordinary return, including any nested loser. These pointers are authored custody, not proof of arbitrary DSO/code/pointee lifetime.
provider_contract.write_args: ap_write_args is a value struct containing int64_t accepted_open_token, size_t requested_length and char payload[33]. Build a zero-initialized local value from the entered WRITE receipt. Pass the copied owner and write args by value so no callback receives a pointer to private working owner/event/raw state. The full 33 canonical owner bytes and write bytes/length stay distinct.
